policy.rule: REQUEST_AUDIO when J(audio) >= tau, else STOP

definition.uncertainty: routing uncertainty under the frozen policy (score_entropy -> llm_normalized_score_entropy), in [0, 1]
definition.score_top2: second largest normalised self-reported class score
definition.score_entropy: Shannon entropy of the normalised score vector, in nats
definition.score_mass_top2: score_top1 + score_top2, how concentrated the answer is
definition.active_score_classes: number of classes given a non-zero score
definition.llm_confidence: the model's own self-reported confidence (NOT a posterior)
definition.llm_evidence_strength: the model's own self-reported evidence strength
definition.predicted_is_<class>: indicator that the LLM currently predicts <class>
definition.note: Every feature is computable at inference time from the LLM response alone. None is derived from a label, from the audio model, or from the fused outcome.

features.imputation: none -- an incomplete row receives no estimate

training_summary.class_imbalance_note: AUPRC is reported alongside AUROC because the positive event is a minority; on an imbalanced target AUROC alone flatters a model that would be useless at the operating point.
training_summary.formula: gain(m | A) = P(correct | A u {m}) - P(correct | A)
training_summary.why_rejected: Stage 1 measured it directly: the sign depends on which modality is the anchor and on the fusion rule, in five of six configurations it was negative while accuracy rose 8-10 points, and its largest per-sample correlation with actual decision improvement was 0.143. See docs/ahsef_stage1.md section 8.2 and experiments/ahsef/stage1/reports/gain_diagnostics_validation.json.

identifying_useful_acquisitions.positive_event: y_gain -- audio fixed a wrong text prediction
identifying_useful_acquisitions.imbalance_note: AUPRC is compared against the base rate, not against 0.5. An AUPRC at or below the base rate means the estimator adds nothing at the operating point regardless of its AUROC.

avoiding_harmful_acquisitions.positive_event: y_harm -- audio broke a correct text prediction
avoiding_harmful_acquisitions.note: Reported as 1 - AUROC because a *useful* estimator should give harmful acquisitions a LOW predicted gain. Values above 0.5 mean it does.

calibration.note: Bins are quantiles of the predicted gain, so each holds a comparable number of samples. A monotone mean_observed_gain across bins is the property routing depends on; the residual column says whether the magnitude is also usable once a cost penalty is subtracted.

selection_rule.primary: highest out-of-fold AUROC against y_gain on validation
selection_rule.tie_break: among variants whose AUROC falls inside the bootstrap 95% interval of the best -- that is, variants this pool cannot distinguish -- prefer 'paired_logistic'.
selection_rule.why_paired_wins_ties: UGAPR computes J = gain - lambda*C - mu*L, so the gain has to be in the units the target is defined in: a DIFFERENCE of probabilities of being correct. paired_logistic emits exactly that. fix_logistic emits P(audio fixes a wrong answer), which lives in [0, 1], is a different quantity, and cannot express harm at all -- subtracting a cost from it would be a category error dressed as a utility. The preference is therefore a property of the estimator's output, not of its score on this pool.

quality.note: Reported quality is OUT OF FOLD. The saved coefficients are refitted on the whole validation split, which is what the router uses; the in-sample quality of that refit is not reported because it would be optimistic.

hsig.formula: gain(m | A) = P(correct | A u {m}) - P(correct | A)
hsig.why_rejected: Stage 1 measured it directly: the sign depends on which modality is the anchor and on the fusion rule, in five of six configurations it was negative while accuracy rose 8-10 points, and its largest per-sample correlation with actual decision improvement was 0.143. See docs/ahsef_stage1.md section 8.2 and experiments/ahsef/stage1/reports/gain_diagnostics_validation.json.

weights.formula: J(m) = gain_hat(m) - lambda * C(m) - mu * L(m)

definition.latency_ms: measured mean per-sample feature extraction + forward pass
definition.compute_units: parameters x input_elements, a MAC-order proxy, not a FLOP count
definition.normalization: each quantity divided per the 'max' rule over the candidate set being ranked

ugapr.note: Utility is computed only when HSIG supplies a gain estimate. With no estimator implemented, UGAPR reports selection_available=False and selects nothing. It never falls back to a cost-only or fixed order.

availability.source: frozen audio prediction set sample ids
availability.unavailable_reason: no audio prediction exists for this sample id
availability.policy: A requested but unavailable modality yields REQUESTED_BUT_UNAVAILABLE. The text-only prediction is kept and no fused prediction is produced. Nothing is zero-filled, uniform-filled, set to neutral, or substituted with another modality.

policy.single_candidate_limitation: The Stage 3 candidate set has exactly one member, because no sample in this project has two simultaneously available candidate modalities. UGAPR therefore demonstrates the accept/reject half of its job -- does the candidate clear its own cost and latency price? -- and NOT the ranking half. Audio is not selected because it is the only option: a sample whose utility falls below the frozen threshold is stopped with audio unacquired, and the ablations report how often that happens.
